trips.name: Grayling trip

house.label: Trip house (Circle Ct, Au Sable)
house.note: Rental on the Au Sable just off M-72 on the west side of Grayling (pin approximate). The river behind the house is Type 1 trout water: open from Apr 24, 2027, worms and spinners legal for the boys. Flies-only water starts ~5 mi downstream at Burton's Landing.

summary: Last Saturday in April 2027 is Apr 24, so the trip (Fri Apr 30 – Sun May 2) is the second weekend of the season.
Kids' water (bait + spinners legal): the house stretch and town water (Type 1/2), East Branch, Bright Lake, Kneff Lake, Howes Lake. Lures-only (spinners, no worms): Manistee CR 612 → M-72.
Adults' fly water: Holy Water (Burton's Landing → Wakeley), Manistee M-72 → CCC, North & South Branch GR reaches — flies only, no beads.
Hendricksons usually come off in the early–mid afternoon in late April/May; median water temps on these dates are ~48–52°F at nearby gages, so afternoons fish best.

Licences: Mark, his brother and brother-in-law each need a 2027 Michigan fishing licence (2026 licences expire Mar 31, 2027). The boys (under 17) need none but must follow the rules. An adult actively helping a child fish should be licensed.
plan: Arrive · settle in · kids fish the house water with worms/spinners until dark; adults scout Burton's Landing (9 min).

AM: Bright Lake pier (stocked rainbows) + East Branch trail walk at Hartwick Pines. Afternoon: dads take turns on the Holy Water for the Hendrickson hatch (1–4 pm) while kids fish the house. Evening: house water.

AM: Manistee — 13-yr-old spins the lures-only reach (CR 612 → M-72); fly guys fish M-72 flies-only. Late AM: Kneff Lake or Howes Lake for the younger boys if the river is slow. Head home after lunch (~3.5 h).

streams.history: Stocked with brook trout 1949–64, when the headwaters were called 'Townsend Creek'; DNR has no record of why it stopped (SR39 p.50). Brook trout were already here before any stocking: University of Michigan museum specimens collected in 1927 at the county-line bridges and in Burr Creek, Bruce Twp. Conservation-officer creel checks logged brookies on opening days 1930–63 (e.g. 48 anglers kept 112 on 4/30/1960; SR39 App. 2). Brown trout were stocked 1971–91 with 'marginal' survival; no trout stocked on the North Branch since 2009 (steelhead) and no brook trout since 1964 (DNR stocking DB). The 2001–02 DNR survey found brook trout only in Kidder Creek (8.6% of the catch at Boardman Rd), none at the three North Branch sites (all below Almont); SR39 still says the North Branch above Almont 'continues to have a self-sustaining brook trout population', and CRWC says native brookies were 'rediscovered' and are being monitored with DNR.
